scope: Follow-up evidence and bibliographic leads; no new observation release
policy: A bibliographic hypothesis never grants measurement compatibility or identity

additional_master_blocks.reviewed: Fomin et al. 2023, Objects and methods sections 2.1-2.2, Table 1 and Figure 1
directly_reported: Daryino/Zelenograd mixed-spruce forest Albic Glossic Retisol, five cores from each of A, E and Bt horizons
Sandbox and kaolinite-sand-box equilibration, followed by saturated-salt vapor equilibration at high pF
Full saturation is denoted pF 0 for graphical representation
unresolved: Exact five-workbook-core identity and A-horizon depth difference: workbook 0-5 cm versus published 0-7 cm
Water denominator and scale for the literal workbook W values
Workbook first-axis 0.01 versus source graphical saturation marker; no finite physical suction is inferred
Branch and replicate identity; vapor-equilibrium potential interpretation before treating all retained coordinates as matric pressure
additional_master_blocks.eligibility_effect: No release; do not transplant related-paper methods or horizon means into individual cores

additional_master_blocks.reviewed: Workbook dissertation-link row 6; raw dissertation and master representations; primary library reference
additional_master_blocks.finding: The workbook retains source-local meter-water-head labels and repeated numeric coordinates, but unit labels alone do not establish branch/sample identity or water-content scale. The linked full experimental document was not retrieved through the available library interface.
additional_master_blocks.required_evidence: Readable original experimental tables/figures, water denominator and scale, wetting/drying and replicate identities, duplicate-coordinate disposition, exact wide/master identity crosswalk

additional_evidence.finding: Methods section 2.2 distinguishes repacked samples, intact cores of several dimensions, field drying experiments, tensiostats and saturated-salt equilibration. It also describes middle-curve reconstruction by the Voronin method. Table 3 reports volumetric fitted saturation parameters, not a point-level measurement crosswalk. These experiment-wide statements do not identify which literal workbook points were measured.

additional_master_blocks.reviewed: Workbook dissertation-link row 19 and raw dissertation blocks; original university listing of the 2012 thesis
additional_master_blocks.finding: The linked dissertation title and author are confirmed by the university, but the accessible descriptions do not supply the exact original retention tables, absolute-water scale and sample/replicate crosswalk for the workbook vectors.
additional_master_blocks.required_evidence: Original retention figures/tables and methods with exact sample and pressure-coordinate mapping

sources.reviewed: Sapozhnikov 1994 original author abstract, hydrophysical properties discussion
sources.finding: The author discusses retention curves against pF, but the reviewed abstract does not identify the exact four workbook curves, their water scale and the centimeter-head definition together.
sources.required_evidence: Original 1987 experimental figure/table with absolute water denominator, scale and pressure definition; exact curve and treatment match

sources.reviewed: Sapozhnikov 1994 original author abstract; existing complete-curve reconstruction
sources.finding: The bijective 12-curve workbook match establishes identity and relative scale only. It does not establish percent-versus-fraction semantics or the physical meaning of the proposed first-axis replacement.
sources.required_evidence: Original 1988 water-axis caption and pressure definition, including saturation convention

sources.bibliographic_hypothesis: Khaydapova and Aksenov, relationship of plastic strength and stickiness with the retention curve, Pochvovedenie 2001(5), 586-593
sources.finding: The related original dissertation is restricted in the RSL access record. Citations do not establish the exact experimental curves, dry-mass scale or source pressure convention. Cached long identifiers also mix master curves.
sources.required_evidence: Accessible original methods/figures and exhaustive point-level identity review

sources.reviewed: Pestonova 2007 original author abstract, Figure 7, printed p.21 / RSL viewer p.23
sources.finding: Dry-mass percent water is already confirmed. Reviewed text layers do not preserve an unambiguous pressure-unit label; local image retrievals contain a gateway error or an empty image. Neither image is scientific evidence.
sources.required_evidence: Readable original pressure-axis caption and physical meaning of the proposed saturation replacement

additional_primary_followup.reviewed: Publisher abstract, author metadata, original Russian citation and access statement
additional_primary_followup.finding: Shvarov and Koreneva (2008) studied capillary-sorption hysteresis in European Russian zonal soils. The original Russian article is Pochvovedenie 10, 1179-1187; the translation is Eurasian Soil Science 41, 1041-1049. The publisher exposes subscription preview content. This confirms a 2008 publication lead, not the exact identities, absolute-water scale or pressure definitions of the 21 workbook rows. Earlier matched difference vectors remain unsuitable as absolute retention measurements.
additional_primary_followup.eligibility_effect: No release; highest conditional source-review ceiling in the current audited roster still requires original experimental tables

sources.reviewed: Earlier Shvarov original author abstract, imprint 1984, Table 2
sources.finding: Two matching complete vectors describe adsorption-desorption differences, not absolute water content. This is a provenance incompatibility independent of scale. Other curves and the 2008 attribution remain unresolved.
sources.required_evidence: Original 2008 absolute-retention tables with exact sample crosswalk; reject confirmed difference vectors as retention targets

sources.finding: The reviewed 2009 chernozem publication concerns carbon dynamics; the separate revegetation paper concerns drilling wastes. Shared author/year and mentions of chernozems do not identify the three workbook centrifugation curves.
sources.required_evidence: Exact original retention figure for the three Kursk land uses, with water basis and pressure-unit definition

sources.bibliographic_hypothesis: Chudinova, Dielectric characteristics of soils and categories of soil water, Eurasian Soil Science 42, 405-414
sources.finding: The publisher abstract names three matching soil types but does not give the W denominator/scale, exact retention pressure coordinates or duplicate-placeholder interpretation. The full experimental article is subscription content.
sources.required_evidence: Original methods and retention figure with exact three-sample match; water and pressure units; first two axis positions

sources.finding: The workbook labels pressure over salts. A relative humidity or salt identity is not interchangeable with a measured matric-potential coordinate. No exact primary table has been identified for these six workbook records.
sources.required_evidence: Exact primary publication, water denominator and scale, salt identities, temperature, equilibrium convention and justified matric-versus-total potential treatment

sources.reviewed: Vasyukov et al. 2012, original pp.67-70, retention figure p.70
sources.finding: The original figure establishes volumetric fractions but labels a logarithm of water potential without a pressure or head unit. The workbook pF label is not independent confirmation.
sources.required_evidence: Source-specific definition of the logarithmic pressure coordinate

sources.bibliographic_hypothesis: Manucharova 2012, Hydrolytic prokaryotic complexes of terrestrial ecosystems, original author abstract
sources.finding: The author/year lead identifies a microbiology dissertation, not an exact methods/table match for the three workbook retention curves. Bibliographic agreement cannot establish dry-mass scale or pressure convention.
sources.required_evidence: Exact original retention experiment, curve identities, dry-mass water scale and pressure convention

sources.reviewed: Shein, Shcheglov and Moskvin 2012; Moskvin 2013 original author abstract
sources.finding: The primary study describes reconstructed retention parameters and van Genuchten approximation. The workbook labels approximation too. Physical unit confirmation cannot turn reconstructed curve points into independent measured observations.
sources.required_evidence: Original figure/table identifying a directly measured subset and exact point-level identity, if one exists

sources.finding: The reviewed thermal-property publication supplies hydrological constants, not a verified pressure grid. A categorical PGK axis is not assigned invented matric pressures.
sources.required_evidence: Exact original constants, water scale and a source-supported pressure condition for each constant; otherwise retain as non-WRC data

sources.finding: The workbook uses the same categorical PGK axis, but its label and similar values do not establish the first Makarychev publication's identity or a continuous pressure coordinate.
sources.required_evidence: Exact original publication and sample crosswalk, water scale and pressure condition for each hydrological constant

sources.bibliographic_hypothesis: Sidorova and Borisova, The flow of moisture in the model sod-podzolic soil under mulch fir litter, 71(2), 63-70
sources.finding: Publisher metadata and abstract describe moisture redistribution under mulch; they do not establish the exact two sparse workbook curves, volumetric scale, pressure convention or saturation replacement.
sources.required_evidence: Original experimental figure and methods with exact two-sample match and pressure-axis definition

sources.bibliographic_hypothesis: Shein and Mady 2018, Hysteresis of the water retention curve: wetting branch simulation based on the drying curve
sources.reviewed: Publisher abstract; Shein 2019 HYDRUS primary paper methods and references
sources.finding: The 2018 publisher abstract directly reports capillarimetry and 0 to -800 cmH2O for wetting/drying branches. It does not identify the four workbook horizons, their water scale or their branch. The 2019 related paper uses a different layer partition. These claims cannot release the 25 workbook points.
sources.required_evidence: Exact original four-horizon table/figure, branch identity, volumetric scale and retained coordinate match
